record.paper_title: Open Questions in Charm Decays Deserving an Answer
record.original_question: Do Cabibbo-suppressed charm decays such as D^0 -> K^+ K^-, D^0 -> pi^+ pi^-, D^+ -> K^+ K^- pi^+, and D^+ -> phi pi^+ show direct CP violation or T-odd final-state correlations at the 10^-3 level, which is roughly the upper size expected within the Standard Model but could be enhanced to about the 1% level by New Physics?

evidence.quote: A rough estimate suggests that within the SM direct CP asymmetries could be as ‘large’ as O(10−3 ) [12, 13].

It is not inconceivable that NP could enhance these asymmetries somewhat, say to the 1% level. Larger effects could surface in the Dalitz plots for D → KKπ, ¯ 3π or in T-odd correlations, like for example h~pπ± · (~pK+ × ~pK− )i in D± → K+K−π ±π 0 .
one should aim for achieving a 10−3 sensitivity for CP asymmetries involving D0 − D¯ 0 oscillations as well as for direct CP violation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider singly Cabibbo-suppressed decays of charmed mesons, in particular the two-body modes $D^0 \to K^+ K^-$ and $D^0 \to \pi^+ \pi^-$, the three-body mode $D^+ \to K^+ K^- \pi^+$ (including its $\phi\pi^+$ resonant component), and four-body modes such as $D^\pm \to K^+ K^- \pi^\pm \pi^0$. For a decay $D \to f$ with CP-conjugate $\bar D \to \bar f$, define the direct CP asymmetry
$$A_{CP}(f) = \frac{\Gamma(D \to f) - \Gamma(\bar D \to \bar f)}{\Gamma(D \to f) + \Gamma(\bar D \to \bar f)},$$
and for the four-body mode define the T-odd triple-product correlation
$$C_T = \langle \vec p_{\pi^\pm} \cdot (\vec p_{K^+} \times \vec p_{K^-}) \rangle,$$
with the CP-violating observable $A_T = \tfrac{1}{2}(C_T - \bar C_T)$ (where $\bar C_T$ is the analogous quantity for the CP-conjugate decay). Within the Standard Model these direct CP asymmetries and T-odd correlations are estimated to be at most of order $10^{-3}$, while New Physics could plausibly enhance them to about the $1\%$ level.

Determine experimentally whether any of these singly Cabibbo-suppressed charm decays exhibits a nonzero direct CP asymmetry $A_{CP}$ or a nonzero T-odd correlation $A_T$ at the $10^{-3}$ sensitivity level, and decide whether the observed effects are consistent with the Standard Model expectation of $\lesssim 10^{-3}$ or instead indicate enhancement (e.g. to the $\sim 1\%$ level) characteristic of New Physics.
artifact.category_tag: CP violation in charm meson decays
artifact.status_search_result: LHCb has reached the $10^{-3}$ sensitivity for direct CP asymmetries in singly Cabibbo-suppressed charm decays, and in 2019 reported the first observation of CP violation in charm via $\Delta A_{CP}$ between $D^0\to K^+K^-$ and $D^0\to\pi^+\pi^-$. Individual asymmetries (e.g. $a^d_{K^+K^-}=(6\pm6)\times10^{-4}$, $a^d_{\pi^+\pi^-}=(22\pm6)\times10^{-4}$) are now measured at this level, and dedicated searches in $D^+\to K^+K^-\pi^+$ and T-odd correlations in $D\to KK\pi\pi$ have been performed without conclusive evidence of New Physics. Whether the observed level is fully Standard-Model or contains a New Physics contribution remains debated, so the underlying question is only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of CP Violation Observables in D+ → K-K+π+ Decays (LHCb)
status_evidence.snippet: Search for CP violation in D+ → K-K+π+ using 5.4 fb^-1; no evidence of CP violation, p-value for CP conservation 8.1%.
status_evidence.claim: Direct CP violation in D+ → K+K-π+ has been searched for at LHCb with no evidence at current sensitivity.

status_evidence.title: Direct CP violation in D decays at LHCb
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews of direct CP asymmetry measurements in D0 → K+K-, π+π- at the 10^-4-10^-3 level.
status_evidence.claim: LHCb has measured individual direct CP asymmetries in D0→K+K- and D0→π+π- at the 10^-3 level.

status_evidence.title: PDG 2024 review: CP Violation in the Quark Sector
status_evidence.snippet: Summary of CP violation observations in charm including ΔA_CP discovery.
status_evidence.claim: Direct CP violation in singly Cabibbo-suppressed charm decays has been observed at the level anticipated.
